### Requirements
1. For each aim, the hypotheses you will be testing, including a description of the outcome(s) and predictor(s) of interest

2. The over-all analysis approach you will be using for each hypothesis

3. How you will approach/incorporate the other data/variables available besides the outcomes and predictors of interest

4. What power/sample size calculations you will conduct for each of the hypotheses of interest

5. Not required for interim, but will be required for final: thoughts on your approach to type I error control.

### Aim 1
Higher baseline cytokine and chemokine levels in circulating plasma, indicators of inflammation, will predict declines in memory consolidation and decreases in AD-signature cortical thickness. Furthermore, greater increases in cytokines and chemokines will be associated with greater declines in episodic memory and cortical thickness. We will evaluate this using general linear models for the decline in THE OUTCOME MEASURES with cytokine and chemokine levels at baseline and the difference between year 0 and year 1, while controlling for age, sex, and WHICHEVER SEEMS MOST IMPORTANT. Cytokine and chemokine models will be run separately.


### Aim 2
We will test our hypothesis of an interaction between peripheral levels of inflammation and amyloid deposition,
such that the presence of both significant amyloid deposition and elevated peripheral inflammatory markers will
be the strongest predictors of memory decline and decline in AD-signature cortical thickness over a one year
period.

### Aim 2 Notes


We will test our hypothesis of an interaction between peripheral levels of inflammation and amyloid deposition,
such that the presence of both significant amyloid deposition and elevated peripheral inflammatory markers will
be the strongest predictors of memory decline and decline in AD-signature cortical thickness over a one year
period. We will evaluate this using general linear models for the decline in THE OUTCOME MEASURES with amyloid deposition, peripheral inflammatory markers, and an interaction between the two, while controlling for age, sex, and WHICHEVER SEEMS MOST IMPORTANT.
